repos.name: luongnv89/claude-howto
repos.description: A visual, example-driven guide to Claude Code — from basic concepts to advanced agents, with copy-paste templates that bring immediate value.
repos.one_liner: A comprehensive, visual guide and template library for mastering Claude Code and building advanced AI agents.
bullets: Built as a modular, example-driven repository for rapid AI agent prototyping.
Focuses on practical implementation of Claude Code for complex automation tasks.
Provides copy-paste templates for immediate integration into developer workflows.
Serves as a high-velocity resource for engineers looking to leverage agentic coding tools.

repos.name: oxc-project/tsrs
repos.description: Rust port of the TypeScript 7 type checker
repos.one_liner: A high-performance Rust-based port of the TypeScript type checker, designed for extreme speed in infrastructure tooling.
bullets: Written in Rust to provide memory safety and massive performance gains over the original TypeScript implementation.
Acts as a foundational infrastructure component for modern JavaScript/TypeScript build tooling.
Enables faster static analysis and type checking for large-scale enterprise codebases.
Critical for developers building high-performance devtools and CI/CD pipelines.

repos.name: gamedev-skills/awesome-gamedev-agent-skills
repos.description: 74 game-dev skills for AI coding agents — Godot, Unity, Unreal, Phaser, PixiJS, three.js, Bevy, pygame, LÖVE, Roblox. Portable SKILL.md Agent Skills (the format Anthropic launched as Claude Skills), with a router that loads the right skill for your engine and task. Runs in Claude Code, Cursor, Kiro, Codex, Copilot, Gemini CLI and more.
repos.one_liner: A curated collection of 74 portable agent skills designed to enable AI coding agents to interact with major game engines.
bullets: Utilizes the Claude Skills format for standardized, portable agent capabilities.
Supports a wide range of engines including Godot, Unity, Unreal, and Bevy.
Facilitates the automation of complex game development tasks via LLM-driven agents.
Provides a structured framework for extending agentic intelligence into specialized technical domains.

repos.name: alexgaoth/awesome-reverse-engineered
repos.description: Don't reverse engineer it twice. 12,000+ open-source tools built by reverse engineering closed apps, APIs, devices, protocols, file formats, games and AI tools. Search site + agent skill, refreshed nightly.
repos.one_liner: A massive, searchable database of 12,000+ open-source tools derived from reverse-engineering closed-source systems.
bullets: Aggregates reverse-engineered protocols, APIs, and file formats into a single searchable index.
Includes agent-ready skills to assist developers in integrating with proprietary or legacy systems.
Highly valuable for fintech and security professionals needing to interface with closed financial APIs.
Reduces redundant engineering effort by documenting existing community-led reverse engineering projects.

repos.name: nano-muse/nanoMuse
repos.description: nanoMuse: an open-source personal agent for every device you own. One agent with a name and a look of its own that does things, keeps working while the app is closed, remembers you, and asks before anything you cannot undo. On Android, iPhone and iPad, Windows / macOS / Linux and in the browser; your phone's screen and your computer as its hands.
repos.one_liner: An open-source, persistent personal agent framework designed to run across multiple devices with long-term memory.
bullets: Built with Swift, focusing on native performance and cross-device synchronization.
Features persistent background operation and long-term memory capabilities for personalized assistance.
Designed as a privacy-conscious, user-controlled agent architecture.
Ideal for building custom personal productivity agents that require context-awareness and cross-platform presence.
